question: Which actinide, discovered by Glenn T Seaborg in 1940, is used as a heat source for sensitive electrical components in satellites as well as a power source for satellites?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Plutonium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plutonium (element 94) was first synthesised and identified in December 1940/1941 by Glenn T. Seaborg and his colleagues (Edwin McMillan, Joseph W. Kennedy, Arthur Wahl) at the University of California, Berkeley. (प्लूटोनियम — ग्लेन सीबॉर्ग द्वारा खोजा गया रेडियोधर्मी तत्व)

 

• Its isotope Plutonium-238 is widely used to make Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs), which convert the heat released by radioactive decay into electricity, powering deep-space probes and satellites (e.g. Voyager, Cassini, New Horizons) where solar power is impractical.

 

• Because of its long half-life and steady heat output, Pu-238 also serves as a compact heat source for keeping sensitive electronic components warm in the cold environment of space.

 

• Seaborg is credited with the discovery of several transuranium (actinide) elements and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1951 jointly with Edwin McMillan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Americium (Option 4), also discovered by Seaborg's team (1944), is mainly used in smoke detectors (Am-241) rather than as a satellite power source.

 

• The actinide series consists of 15 elements from Actinium (89) to Lawrencium (103), most of which are radioactive and man-made.

 

NOTE

 

• Curium (Option 1): Discovered in 1944, named after Marie and Pierre Curie; used in some scientific instruments, not the primary satellite power/heat source.

 

• Nobelium (Option 3): A synthetic actinide with no significant power-generation application; used only for research purposes.

 

• Americium (Option 4): Chiefly used in ionisation-type smoke detectors, not as the standard RTG fuel for satellites — that role belongs to Plutonium-238.

question: The Jagannath Temple in Puri depicts which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Odissi is one of the oldest surviving classical dance forms of India, originating in the temples of Odisha, especially the Jagannath Temple, Puri, where it developed as a temple dance (mahari/gotipua tradition). (ओडिसी नृत्य — जगन्नाथ मंदिर, पुरी)

 

• Sculptural evidence of Odissi dance postures is found carved on the walls of Odisha's temples, including at Puri and the Sun Temple, Konark.

 

• Odissi is characterised by the tribhangi (three-bend) posture and fluid, sculpturesque body movements depicting devotion to Lord Jagannath (Krishna/Vishnu).

 

• Noted exponents of Odissi include Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh and Sanjukta Panigrahi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has eight classical dance forms recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu, associated with temples like the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 1): Originated in Andhra Pradesh, rooted in the Bhagavata Mela tradition.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 2): Originated in Tamil Nadu temples, not associated with Puri's Jagannath Temple.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): Originated in North India, associated with storytelling (katha) traditions of temples and later royal courts, not Puri.

question: Who among the following IPS officers in 2023 is one of the first women officers to become the Director General of police in Punjab?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shashi Prabha Dwivedi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In January 2023, IPS officer Shashi Prabha Dwivedi, along with Gurpreet Kaur Deo, became one of the first two women officers to be promoted to the rank of Director General of Police (DGP) in Punjab, when seven officers of the Punjab cadre were elevated to DGP rank. (शशि प्रभा द्विवेदी — पंजाब की पहली महिला DGP में से एक)

 

• This promotion marked a historic first for women IPS officers in the Punjab Police hierarchy, which had never before had a woman hold the DGP rank.

 

• Shashi Prabha Dwivedi is a senior IPS officer of the 1989 batch, Punjab cadre.

 

• The promotion was made by the Punjab government's Department of Personnel in line with the Punjab Police Service rules for elevation to the highest rank.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gurpreet Kaur Deo was the other woman IPS officer promoted to DGP rank in Punjab at the same time (January 2023).

 

• The Director General of Police (DGP) is the highest-ranking police officer in an Indian state, heading the state police force.

 

NOTE

 

• Meera Chadha Borwankar (Option 2): A retired 1981-batch IPS officer of the Maharashtra cadre, first woman to head Mumbai's Crime Branch; not connected to Punjab's 2023 DGP promotions.

 

• Aparajita Rai (Option 3): A well-known IPS officer from Sikkim, not part of the Punjab DGP promotions.

 

• Ruveda Salam (Option 4): The first Muslim woman IPS officer from Jammu and Kashmir, unrelated to the Punjab DGP appointment.

question: A natural process of mechanical disintegration and or chemical decomposition of the rocks of the crust of the Earth by certain physical and chemical agencies of the atmosphere is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is weathering.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Weathering is the in-situ mechanical disintegration and/or chemical decomposition of rocks at or near the Earth's surface due to atmospheric agents such as temperature change, water, wind, and biological activity. (अपक्षय — चट्टानों का टूटना/विघटन)

 

• Weathering is broadly classified into physical (mechanical) weathering, chemical weathering, and biological weathering.

 

• Unlike erosion, weathering does not involve the transport of the broken-down material — it happens where the rock is located.

 

• Weathering is the first step in soil formation (pedogenesis), breaking parent rock into regolith that later develops into soil.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Exfoliation, hydrolysis, oxidation, carbonation and hydration are common processes involved in weathering.

 

• Erosion, by contrast, involves both the breakdown and the transport of rock material by agents like water, wind, and ice.

 

NOTE

 

• Solidification of rocks (Option 1): Refers to the cooling and hardening of molten magma/lava into igneous rock, unrelated to disintegration.

 

• Mew rock formation (Option 3): Not a recognised geological term/process.

 

• Watering of rocks (Option 4): Not a standard geological term; water is only one of several agents involved in weathering, not a process by itself.

question: In T20 cricket matches, a bowler can bowl a maximum of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4 overs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Twenty20 (T20) cricket, each innings consists of a maximum of 20 overs per side, and as per ICC playing conditions, a single bowler may bowl a maximum of 4 overs in an innings. (टी20 क्रिकेट — एक गेंदबाज अधिकतम 4 ओवर)

 

• This 4-over limit ensures that at least 5 different bowlers are typically required to complete a 20-over innings.

 

• In ODIs (50 overs), the maximum per bowler is 10 overs; in Test cricket, there is no restriction on the number of overs a bowler can bowl.

 

• If a match is shortened due to weather (e.g., a Duckworth-Lewis-Stern revised T20 match), the maximum overs per bowler is adjusted proportionally (usually to one-fifth of the revised overs).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• T20 cricket was first introduced by the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) in 2003.

 

• The inaugural ICC Men's T20 World Cup was held in South Africa in 2007, won by India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (7, 6, 5 overs) are incorrect because none of these matches the ICC-mandated per-bowler over limit of 4 overs in a 20-over T20 innings.

question: Who among the following served the shortest tenure as the Prime Minister of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandra Shekhar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chandra Shekhar served as India's 8th Prime Minister from 10 November 1990 to 21 June 1991, a tenure of only about 223 days, the shortest among the four options given. (चंद्रशेखर — सबसे कम कार्यकाल वाले प्रधानमंत्रियों में से एक)

 

• He headed a minority government (Samajwadi Janata Party) with outside support from the Congress, which was withdrawn, forcing his resignation.

 

• HD Deve Gowda was PM from June 1996 to April 1997 (about 324 days); VP Singh from December 1989 to November 1990 (about 343 days); IK Gujral from April 1997 to March 1998 (about 332 days) — all longer than Chandra Shekhar's tenure.

 

• Note that the overall shortest-ever tenure as Indian PM was held by Gulzarilal Nanda, who twice served briefly as acting Prime Minister (13 days each, in 1964 and 1966), though he is not among the given options.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's longest-serving Prime Minister is Jawaharlal Nehru (over 16 years, 1947-1964), followed by Indira Gandhi and Narendra Modi.

 

• Chandra Shekhar contested elections from Ballia, Uttar Pradesh, and was known as the "Young Turk" of Indian politics.

 

NOTE

 

• HD Deva Gowda (Option 1): Served roughly 324 days (June 1996-April 1997) — longer than Chandra Shekhar's tenure.

 

• VP Singh (Option 2): Served roughly 343 days (December 1989-November 1990) — longer than Chandra Shekhar's tenure.

 

• IK Gujral (Option 4): Served roughly 332 days (April 1997-March 1998) — longer than Chandra Shekhar's tenure.

question: In which year India won gold in men’s hockey in the Olympic games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1980.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won the gold medal in men's hockey at the 1980 Moscow Olympics, defeating Spain 4-3 in the final. (भारत — 1980 मास्को ओलंपिक हॉकी स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• This was India's 8th Olympic gold medal in men's hockey, and remained India's last Olympic hockey gold until the 2020 Tokyo Olympics bronze broke a long medal drought (India won bronze in Tokyo 2020, not gold).

 

• India's earlier hockey gold medals came in 1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964 and 1980.

 

• The 1980 Moscow Games were boycotted by several Western nations, which affected the competition field, but the gold remains an official Olympic gold medal for India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Legendary hockey player Major Dhyan Chand was a key figure in India's dominant hockey era (1928-1936 golds).

 

• India's men's hockey team won a bronze medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held in 2021) and another bronze at Paris 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• 1984 (Option 1): India did not win hockey gold in 1984; the USA won that year at the Los Angeles Olympics (which the USSR bloc boycotted).

 

• 1992 (Option 2): India did not win hockey gold in 1992 (Germany won at Barcelona).

 

• 1988 (Option 4): India did not win hockey gold in 1988 (Great Britain won at Seoul).

question: Name the longest highway single-tube tunnel that reduces the travel time and overall distance between Manali and Keylong.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atal Tunnel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Atal Tunnel (Rohtang Tunnel), inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi on 3 October 2020, is a 9.02 km long single-tube highway tunnel built under the Rohtang Pass in the Pir Panjal range, Himachal Pradesh. (अटल सुरंग — मनाली-केलांग दूरी में कमी)

 

• It connects Manali to the Lahaul-Spiti valley (via Keylong), reducing the road distance by about 46 km and providing all-weather connectivity that was earlier cut off for nearly 6 months a year due to snow at Rohtang Pass.

 

• At an altitude of 3,000+ metres, it is recognised as the longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet (3,000 m) in the world.

 

• It was named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, who had approved the project.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tunnel is built using the Austrian tunnelling method and is horseshoe-shaped.

 

• Other notable Himalayan tunnels include the Zoji La Tunnel (Jammu & Kashmir-Ladakh) and Sela Tunnel (Arunachal Pradesh).

 

NOTE

 

• Natuwadi Tunnel (Option 2) and Karbude Tunnel (Option 3): Located on the Mumbai-Goa (Konkan) highway in Maharashtra, unrelated to the Manali-Keylong route.

 

• Jawahar Tunnel (Option 4): Located on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway through the Pir Panjal range (Banihal Pass), not connected to Manali-Keylong.

question: Which institution launched the Self-Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme in 1992-93?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Self-Help Group (SHG) - Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP) was launched by NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) in 1992 as a pilot project. (नाबार्ड — स्वयं सहायता समूह-बैंक संबद्धता कार्यक्रम)

 

• It is aimed at providing formal banking services to the rural poor, especially women, by linking informal Self-Help Groups with the formal banking system.

 

• It is recognised as the world's largest microfinance programme in terms of the number of clients served.

 

• NABARD was established in 1982 based on the recommendations of the Shivaraman Committee, and functions as an apex development bank for agriculture and rural development in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD is headquartered in Mumbai.

 

• NABARD also runs the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) to support rural infrastructure projects.

 

NOTE

 

• SBI (Option 1): India's largest public sector bank; participates as a lending bank under SBLP but did not launch the programme.

 

• SIDBI (Option 3): Small Industries Development Bank of India, focused on financing MSMEs, not the launcher of SBLP.

 

• IDBI (Option 4): Industrial Development Bank of India, focused on industrial financing, not the launcher of SBLP.

question: In February 2022, West Bengal government launched an open-air classroom programme for students from Class 1 to 7, by the name ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paray Shikshalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The West Bengal government launched the "Paray Shikshalaya" (meaning "school in the neighbourhood/locality") programme in February 2022, an open-air classroom initiative for students of Classes 1 to 7. (पाड़ा शिक्षालय — पश्चिम बंगाल की खुली कक्षा योजना)

 

• The programme was launched to help students, especially those without digital access, cope with learning loss caused by prolonged COVID-19 school closures.

 

• Classes were held in open community spaces such as parks, courtyards and verandas, along with distribution of mid-day meals, following COVID-appropriate norms.

 

• The scheme was implemented under the West Bengal School Education Department.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Union Ministry of Education, covering school education from pre-school to senior secondary level across India, not specific to West Bengal.

 

• SHREYAS (Scheme for Higher Education Youth in Apprenticeship and Skills) is a central government scheme related to apprenticeship and employability for students.

 

NOTE

 

• Shiksha Abhiyan (Option 1): Not the specific name of West Bengal's February 2022 open-air classroom scheme.

 

• Samagra Shiksha (Option 2): A national umbrella scheme of the Central Government, not West Bengal's state-specific open-air classroom initiative.

 

• SHREYAS (Option 3): A central scheme for apprenticeship/employability of graduates, unrelated to open-air classrooms for Classes 1-7.

question: Ricky Kej won his third Grammy award in 2023 for which of the following albums?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Divine Tides.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian composer Ricky Kej won his third Grammy Award at the 65th Annual Grammy Awards (held on 5 February 2023) in the Best Immersive Audio Album category for the album "Divine Tides", created with former Police drummer Stewart Copeland. (रिकी केज — तीसरा ग्रैमी पुरस्कार, 'डिवाइन टाइड्स' एल्बम)

 

• His first Grammy came in 2015 for "Winds of Samsara" (with Wouter Kellerman) in the Best New Age Album category.

 

• His second Grammy was also for "Divine Tides", won in the Best New Age Album category at the same 65th Grammy Awards ceremony (2023) — making Divine Tides a double Grammy-winning album for him at that ceremony, and "Divine Tides" is thus correctly linked to his third overall Grammy win.

 

• Ricky Kej is also a well-known environmentalist and a UNEP Goodwill Ambassador.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ricky Kej is based in Bengaluru, Karnataka, and is known for blending Indian classical/world music with environmental themes.

 

• He later won a fourth Grammy in 2024 for the album "Chapter 2: Wild Terrain" in the Best New Age, Ambient or Chant Album category.

 

NOTE

 

• Winds of Samsara (Option 1): This was the album for which Ricky Kej won his first Grammy (2015), not his third.

 

• Ballad of Maya (Option 2): Not a Ricky Kej Grammy-winning album.

 

• Mann Mein Aman (Option 4): Not the album associated with Ricky Kej's 2023 Grammy win.

question: The Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kutch and Sundarbans region provide ideal conditions for utilising _________ energy in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is tidal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tidal energy is harnessed by using the rise and fall of ocean tides to generate electricity, and requires locations with a high tidal range (large difference between high and low tide). (ज्वारीय ऊर्जा — खंभात की खाड़ी, कच्छ की खाड़ी, सुंदरबन)

 

• The Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay) and the Gulf of Kutch in Gujarat, along with the Sundarbans delta region in West Bengal, have significant tidal ranges, making them the most promising sites in India for tidal power generation.

 

• India's first (pilot-scale) tidal energy project was proposed at the Gulf of Kutch (Durgaduani Creek, Sundarbans) and the Gulf of Khambhat.

 

• Tidal energy is a form of renewable, predictable ocean energy, unlike wind or solar which are more weather-dependent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's potential for wind energy is concentrated in states like Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, and Rajasthan due to favourable wind corridors.

 

• Wave energy and Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) are other forms of ocean-based renewable energy being explored in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Wind (Option 1): Best suited to open plains/coastal corridors with strong sustained winds, not specifically the tidal-range gulfs mentioned.

 

• Thermal (Option 2): Relates to conventional coal/gas-based power generation or OTEC using ocean temperature gradients, not tidal-range locations.

 

• Solar (Option 4): Best suited to regions with high solar insolation like Rajasthan, not specifically tied to these gulf/delta locations.

question: The Lomas Rishi cave which is a manmade cave is located in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lomas Rishi Cave is a rock-cut cave located in the Barabar Hills, in the Jehanabad district of Bihar, dating to the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE), associated with Ashoka. (लोमस ऋषि गुफा — बिहार, बराबर पहाड़ियाँ)

 

• It is famous for its ornamental facade resembling a chaitya-arch entrance, considered one of the earliest examples of rock-cut architecture in India.

 

• The cave was originally dedicated to the Ajivika sect, an ascetic religious order contemporary with Buddhism and Jainism.

 

• Along with other caves in the Barabar and Nagarjuni hills (e.g. Sudama Cave, Karan Chaupar), it represents some of India's earliest surviving examples of rock-cut cave architecture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Barabar Caves were patronised by Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha Maurya, as recorded in inscriptions found there.

 

• The facade style of Lomas Rishi cave later influenced the design of later Buddhist chaitya halls, such as at Ajanta and Karle.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Home to famous rock-cut caves like Ajanta, Ellora and Karle, but not the Lomas Rishi cave.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Known for structural temples (Badami, Aihole, Pattadakal), not the Lomas Rishi cave.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Home to rock-cut/structural sites like Udayagiri and Bhimbetka, but not the Lomas Rishi cave.

question: Commercialisation of agriculture is an indication of ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is marketable surplus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Commercialisation of agriculture refers to farmers producing crops primarily for sale in the market rather than for self-consumption, and is thus indicated by a growing marketable surplus. (विपणन योग्य अधिशेष — वाणिज्यिक कृषि का संकेत)

 

• Marketable surplus is the portion of agricultural produce that remains with the farmer after meeting their own consumption, farm needs, and payments in kind, which is then available to be sold in the market.

 

• As farming shifts from subsistence to a market/commercial orientation, the marketable surplus tends to increase, reflecting a rise in agricultural commercialisation.

 

• Commercialisation of agriculture in India has historical roots in the colonial period, when cash crops (cotton, indigo, jute) were promoted for export rather than food security.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Terms like consumer surplus and producer surplus are concepts from microeconomics/welfare economics, referring to the difference between what consumers/producers are willing to pay/accept versus the market price — unrelated to agricultural commercialisation.

 

• Green Revolution (1960s) significantly boosted marketable surplus of foodgrains in India, especially wheat and rice.

 

NOTE

 

• Income surplus (Option 1): Not a standard term describing agricultural commercialisation.

 

• Producers' surplus (Option 2): A microeconomic welfare concept (area between supply curve and market price), unrelated to commercialisation of agriculture.

 

• Consumer surplus (Option 3): A microeconomic welfare concept (difference between willingness to pay and actual price paid by consumers), unrelated to agricultural commercialisation.

question: The first day of the Tamil calendar on 14 April is celebrated as________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puthandu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Puthandu (also called Puthuvarudam or Tamil New Year) marks the first day of the Tamil calendar, celebrated on 14 April (the first day of the Tamil month of Chithirai). (पुथांडु — तमिल नववर्ष)

 

• It is celebrated with the preparation of "Kanni" (an auspicious tray of items viewed first thing in the morning), a special festive meal, and visits to temples.

 

• Puthandu coincides with New Year celebrations in several other regions on the same date, such as Vishu (Kerala), Poila Boishakh (Bengal), Bihu (Assam), and Vaisakhi (Punjab), since it follows the solar/Mesha Sankranti calendar.

 

• The festival symbolises new beginnings, and homes are decorated with kolam (rangoli) patterns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahamaham is a festival held once every 12 years at Kumbakonam, Tamil Nadu, unrelated to the Tamil New Year.

 

• Pongal is the Tamil harvest festival celebrated in mid-January, marking the Tamil month of Thai.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahamaham (Option 1): A 12-yearly religious bathing festival at Kumbakonam, not the Tamil New Year.

 

• Onam (Option 2): The harvest festival of Kerala, celebrated in August-September, not on 14 April.

 

• Pongal (Option 3): Tamil Nadu's harvest festival, celebrated in mid-January, not 14 April.

question: Identify an endoparasite found in animals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flatworms.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Flatworms (Phylum Platyhelminthes), such as tapeworms (Taenia) and liver flukes (Fasciola), are classic examples of endoparasites — organisms that live inside the body of a host animal, deriving nourishment from it. (चपटे कृमि — प्राणियों के अंतःपरजीवी)

 

• Endoparasites typically inhabit the intestines, liver, blood, or other internal organs of the host, and often have complex life cycles involving intermediate hosts.

 

• Many flatworms show adaptations for a parasitic lifestyle, such as hooks and suckers for attachment, and loss of a digestive system (in tapeworms), absorbing nutrients directly through their body surface.

 

• Examples of common flatworm endoparasites affecting humans/animals include Taenia solium (pork tapeworm) and Schistosoma (blood fluke).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ectoparasites, in contrast, live on the outer surface of the host (e.g., lice, ticks, fleas).

 

• Roundworms (Nematoda), like Ascaris and Wuchereria, are another major group of endoparasites.

 

NOTE

 

• Pleurobrachia (Option 1): A free-living marine ctenophore (comb jelly), not a parasite.

 

• Ctenoplana (Option 2): A free-living, flattened marine ctenophore, not a parasite.

 

• Adamsia (Option 4): A sea anemone that lives in a mutualistic/commensal relationship with hermit crabs (epizoic), not a parasite.

question: The compound in which a hydroxy group, -OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has two other carbon atoms attached to it is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is secondary alcohol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alcohols are classified based on the type of carbon atom to which the -OH (hydroxyl) group is attached. (द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉल — दो अन्य कार्बन परमाणुओं से जुड़ा कार्बन)

 

• In a secondary (2°) alcohol, the carbon bearing the -OH group is attached to exactly two other carbon atoms (e.g., isopropanol/2-propanol, CH3-CHOH-CH3).

 

• In a primary (1°) alcohol, the -OH-bearing carbon is attached to only one other carbon atom (or none, as in methanol).

 

• In a tertiary (3°) alcohol, the -OH-bearing carbon is attached to three other carbon atoms (e.g., tert-butanol).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The general formula for saturated monohydric alcohols is CnH2n+1OH.

 

• The class of an alcohol (1°, 2°, or 3°) affects its oxidation products: primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes then carboxylic acids; secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones; tertiary alcohols resist oxidation under normal conditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Aldehyde (Option 1): Contains a -CHO (carbonyl) group, not a hydroxyl group attached to a saturated carbon; formed by oxidation of primary alcohols.

 

• Tertiary alcohol (Option 2): Has the -OH carbon attached to three other carbon atoms, not two.

 

• Primary alcohol (Option 4): Has the -OH carbon attached to only one (or zero) other carbon atom(s), not two.

question: Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibushan awardee, Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, was instrumental in reviving which of the following classical dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926-2004) was a legendary dance guru from Odisha, widely credited with reviving and reconstructing the classical dance form of Odissi in the mid-20th century after it had declined. (गुरु केलुचरण महापात्र — ओडिसी नृत्य के पुनरुद्धारक)

 

• He was a recipient of the Padma Shri (1975), Padma Bhushan (1988) and posthumously the Padma Vibhushan (2019).

 

• He trained many renowned Odissi dancers, including Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi, Kumkum Mohanty, and his own son Ratikant Mohapatra.

 

• He drew on the temple traditions of the Jagannath Temple, Puri and the folk Gotipua tradition to systematise Odissi into its present classical form.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kelucharan Mohapatra Award is instituted in Odisha in his memory, given to outstanding dancers.

 

• He was also an accomplished Mardala (Odissi percussion) player.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 2): Associated with revivalists like Vedantam Lakshminarayana Sastry and Vempati Chinna Satyam, not Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 3): Associated with revivalists like Rukmini Devi Arundale and the Tanjore Quartet, not Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Manipuri (Option 4): Associated with gurus of the Manipuri tradition (e.g. Guru Bipin Singh), not Kelucharan Mohapatra.

question: Which of the following is mentioned in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
option_1: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Preamble to the Constitution of India exactly states that citizens are secured: "LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship". (उद्देशिका — विचार, अभिव्यक्ति, विश्वास, धर्म और उपासना की स्वतंत्रता)

 

• The Preamble also secures "EQUALITY of status and of opportunity" (not "employment"), "JUSTICE, social, economic and political" (not "administrative"), and "FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation" (not merely "human dignity").

 

• The exact, verbatim wording of the Preamble matters in such questions — only Option 1 reproduces its phrase without alteration.

 

• The Preamble was amended once by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, adding the words "SOCIALIST", "SECULAR" and "INTEGRITY".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble declares India to be a "SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC".

 

• The Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946.

 

NOTE

 

• Fraternity assuring human dignity (Option 2): The actual text reads "Fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation" — this option's wording is incomplete/altered.

 

• Equality of status and employment (Option 3): The actual text reads "Equality of status and of opportunity", not "employment".

 

• Justice, social, economic and administrative (Option 4): The actual text reads "Justice, social, economic and political", not "administrative".

question: Who among the following wrote ‘Anand Math’ from where India’s National song ‘Vande Mataram’ has been taken?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee (Chattopadhyay) wrote the Bengali novel "Anandamath", published in 1882, which contains the song "Vande Mataram", later adopted as India's National Song. (बंकिम चंद्र चटर्जी — आनंदमठ, वंदे मातरम्)

 

• "Vande Mataram" was first sung publicly at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress by Rabindranath Tagore.

 

• The song was formally adopted as the National Song of India by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950, the same day the National Anthem (Jana Gana Mana) was adopted.

 

• "Anandamath" is set during the Sannyasi Rebellion and is regarded as an early influential text of Indian nationalism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rabindranath Tagore wrote India's National Anthem, "Jana Gana Mana", and Bangladesh's national anthem too.

 

• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee is also known for other Bengali novels such as Durgeshnandini and Kapalkundala.

 

NOTE

 

• Abanindranath Tagore (Option 1): A renowned artist and founder of the Bengal School of Art, not the writer of Anandamath.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 2): Wrote India's National Anthem (Jana Gana Mana), not Anandamath; he was the first to sing Vande Mataram publicly.

 

• Mohammad Iqbal (Option 3): Wrote "Saare Jahan Se Achha", not Anandamath.

question: In September 2022, who among the following was appointed as Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lt General Anil Chauhan (Retired).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lieutenant General Anil Chauhan (Retired) was appointed as India's second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) on 28 September 2022. (अनिल चौहान — भारत के दूसरे रक्षा प्रमुख)

 

• He took over the post after it had remained vacant for about nine months, following the death of India's first CDS, General Bipin Rawat, in a helicopter crash on 8 December 2021.

 

• Before his appointment as CDS, Lt Gen Anil Chauhan had earlier served as the Eastern Army Commander and as Director General of Military Operations (DGMO).

 

• The CDS also heads the Department of Military Affairs (DMA) and acts as the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The post of CDS was created in December 2019 following the recommendations of the Kargil Review Committee, to ensure better coordination among the three armed services.

 

• General Bipin Rawat was India's first CDS (took charge 1 January 2020).

 

NOTE

 

• General Manoj Mukund Naravane (Option 1): Served as the 28th Chief of the Army Staff, not CDS.

 

• General Dalbir Singh Suhag (Option 2): A former Chief of the Army Staff (2014-2016), not CDS.

 

• General Manoj Pande (Option 4): Serving as the Chief of the Army Staff (from April 2022), not the CDS.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which state of India has the highest Hindu population percentage of the total population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Himachal Pradesh recorded the highest percentage of Hindu population among Indian states, at approximately 95% of its total population. (हिमाचल प्रदेश — सबसे अधिक हिंदू जनसंख्या प्रतिशत)

 

• Among the given options, the approximate Hindu population percentages (2011 Census) are: Himachal Pradesh ~95%, Odisha ~94%, Chhattisgarh ~93%, Madhya Pradesh ~91%, with Himachal Pradesh ranking highest.

 

• Himachal Pradesh has a small tribal and minority population, contributing to its high Hindu percentage share.

 

• Other states/UTs with notably high Hindu population shares include Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, Hindus form about 79.8% of India's total population nationally.

 

• States/UTs with the lowest Hindu population percentages include Lakshadweep, Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Mizoram, Nagaland and Meghalaya.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 1): Has a high Hindu percentage (~93%) but lower than Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Odisha (Option 2): Has a high Hindu percentage (~94%) but lower than Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Has a Hindu percentage of about 91%, lower than the other three options.

question: The characteristic garlicky odour of garlic is due to _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sulphur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The characteristic pungent smell of garlic is due to sulphur-containing compounds, primarily allicin, which is formed when the enzyme alliinase acts on the compound alliin upon crushing or cutting garlic. (सल्फर — लहसुन की गंध का कारण)

 

• Allicin further breaks down into other organosulphur compounds such as diallyl disulphide, contributing to garlic's distinctive odour and many of its antimicrobial properties.

 

• Garlic (Allium sativum) belongs to the same family as onions, which also owe their pungency to sulphur compounds.

 

• These sulphur compounds are also linked to garlic's reported medicinal properties, such as antibacterial and cholesterol-lowering effects.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Onions release syn-propanethial-S-oxide, a sulphur compound, when cut, which irritates the eyes and causes tears.

 

• Sulphur is an essential element found in amino acids like cysteine and methionine.

 

NOTE

 

• Iodine (Option 1): Essential for thyroid hormone synthesis; not responsible for garlic's odour.

 

• Copper (Option 2): A trace mineral involved in enzyme function; not responsible for garlic's odour.

 

• Chlorine (Option 3): A halogen used as a disinfectant/in table salt (as chloride); not responsible for garlic's odour.

question: Who among the following revolted against Balban, Sultan of Delhi, and declared himself as an independent ruler of Bengal in 1279?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tughril Beg.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tughril Beg (Tughril Khan), the governor of Bengal (Lakhnauti) under Sultan Ghiyasuddin Balban of the Delhi Sultanate, revolted in 1279 and declared himself an independent ruler, even assuming the royal title. (तुगरिल बेग — बंगाल में बलबन के विरुद्ध विद्रोह, 1279)

 

• Balban personally led a large army to suppress the rebellion; Tughril fled but was eventually captured and executed by Balban's forces, led by his son Bughra Khan.

 

• After crushing the revolt, Balban appointed his own son, Bughra Khan, as the governor of Bengal to prevent further uprisings.

 

• This episode highlights Balban's stern, centralising approach to governance and his policy of "blood and iron" to suppress rebellious nobles and provincial governors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1266 to 1287 and is known for strengthening the monarchy and crushing the Chahalgani (Group of Forty nobles).

 

• Bengal remained a frequently rebellious province of the Delhi Sultanate due to its distance from the capital, leading to repeated assertions of independence by its governors.

 

NOTE

 

• Muhammad Khan (Option 1): Balban's eldest son, who died fighting the Mongols in 1285; not connected to the Bengal revolt.

 

• Bughra Khan (Option 3): Balban's second son who was sent to suppress the Bengal revolt and was later made governor of Bengal — he did not lead the revolt himself.

 

• Nasir-ud-din Mahmud (Option 4): An earlier Delhi Sultanate ruler (Balban's predecessor/patron, r. 1246-1266), not connected with the 1279 Bengal revolt.

question: Which of the following organisations was established in 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian National Congress.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885 by Allan Octavian Hume, along with prominent Indians such as Dadabhai Naoroji and Dinshaw Wacha. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस — 1885 में स्थापना)

 

• Its first session was held in Bombay (Mumbai) in December 1885 under the presidency of Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee, with 72 delegates attending.

 

• The INC went on to become the principal vehicle of India's freedom struggle, leading major movements such as the Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, and Quit India movements.

 

• The INC is often described as having originated under the "safety-valve theory", though this remains a debated historiographical view.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The All India Muslim League was founded later, in 1906, at Dhaka.

 

• The Communist Party of India (CPI) was founded in 1925 at Kanpur.

 

NOTE

 

• Communist Party of India (Option 1): Founded in 1925, not 1885.

 

• Muslim League (Option 2): Founded in 1906, not 1885.

 

• East India Organization (Option 3): Not a recognised historical Indian political organisation established in 1885.
